items.title: Russia-Aligned Hackers Use GuardBreaker Prompt Injection to Disrupt AI Malware Analysis
items.description: Russia-aligned operators are testing a new way to make artificial intelligence overlook malicious code. The technique, called GuardBreaker, hides a safety-sensitive request inside an otherwise ordinary script comment, hoping that an AI code scanner refuses to continue its work. items.title: New KATARU IoT Malware Packs Linux Privilege Escalation Exploits and Mirai-Style DDoS Attacks
items.description: KATARU is a newly observed IoT malware strain that can turn poorly secured devices into DDoS attack nodes. The sample was captured after an attacker used repeated Telnet password guesses against a honeypot, then downloaded an ARM payload. It shows how old entry points still give attackers a foothold. items.title: How Threat Actors Are Turning Trusted AI Platforms Into an Attack Surface
items.description: Threat actors are abusing trusted AI platforms to host malicious content, poison search results, and trick users into installing malware. Huntress examines campaigns targeting AI users through weaponized Claude Artifacts, shared AI conversations, sponsored search results, and ClickFix-style lures. [...]

items.title: Hackers Impersonate CEOs in 1 Million Emails to Trick Employees Into $50,000 Payments
items.description: A large email fraud campaign used fake CEO messages and invoices to push employees toward payments of nearly $50,000. The operation did not rely on a malicious attachment or software flaw. Instead, it used ordinary email to deliver a scam. The attackers sent over one million messages to users between August 3 and 5. items.title: Windows 11 Security Update KB5124008 Breaks Always-On VPN Connections
items.description: Microsoft’s September 2026 security update KB5124008 is knocking some Windows 11 enterprise clients off Always On VPN after the Patch Tuesday package landed on September 8. items.title: Attackers Chain JFrog Artifactory Flaws to Gain Admin Control and Plant Backdoors
items.description: Attackers have chained two flaws in JFrog Artifactory, the repository that software build pipelines pull from, to take administrator control of self-hosted servers and plant backdoors, cloud security company Wiz said in a report. Wiz saw the attacks between August 15 and September 8. JFrog had fixed both flaws before then, so only servers that had not been updated were open to them.
